messages.subject: Re: GPS data from bluetooth trackers
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yuen,

I assume the Acc column is some kind of location (in)accuracy estimate. If you are going to be using high resolution data like this, then you will need to use this column to construct an error model. I don't know what the documentation says is the interpretation of this column, but the uere()<- assignment is coded for sqrt(VAR[x]+VAR[y]), which is the convention in engineering. The documentation may contain the exact meaning or calibration data could fit it empirically.

I suspect the area estimates look bad because the lack of an error model is throwing the model off, but I can't say for certain. Variogram plots would help diagnosis if an error model doesn't fix things.

Another thing to check for is that cats have a habit of lying around for long periods of time. You might need to segment the data for just when they are on the move.

Regarding the computational time, the basic algorithms are linear in time, so 10x more data will take 10x longer to run. 14k locations should take a matter of hours (longer with the error model). I have users that analyze millions of locations per individuals, which takes days and needs to be parallelized over individuals to get everything done. You can turn the progress bar on with verbose. You can also thin the data down to a lower frequency than 1Hz - that frequency of information should have a very marginal contribution to the home-range estimate.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: GPS data from bluetooth trackers
messages.body_plain:
To answer the last question in its own post:

BBMM is never the answer for home-range estimation, no matter what the situation is. It's targeting the wrong distribution.
BBMM is the same as ctmm::occurrence() but using Brownian motion (which you can fit in ctmm) instead of a selected movement model that might be different from Brownian motion. The occurrence distribution is appropriate if you want to look at resource utilization - not predict space use (future and past). If you want to predict space use, then you want to use KDE, AKDE, iRSF-AKDE, depending on autocorrelation and selection strength.

https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ecy.70300?af=R

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] rsf.fit vs rsf.select
messages.body_plain:
Hi Laura,

If everywhere is in one of the 3 categories, then they are colinear as CAT1+CAT2+CAT3=1 everywhere.

If the selected model has no selection coefficients, then either selection was weak or there wasn't enough data to resolve it. You can see in the confidence intervals of the second model - are they so wide that they contain substantial values or not.

Negative betas on a categorical means that the reference category is being positively selected and these other categories are being negatively selected. They are relative to each other.

Best,
Chris

This often happens, for example, when a specific cover type is not in an animal's home range, or occurs very rarely. No need for a secondary rsf.fit() command.
> >
> > When using cover type data, remember that the coefficients are in comparison to a reference category (i.e., whatever cover type(s) is/are left out). A positive number is not selection for that coefficient--it is selection compared to the baseline reference category. I generally advise that folks make sure their reference category is relatively large (i.e., contains > 25% or so of an animal's locations, which ensures that selection for the reference category is well-estimated) and is visited roughly in proportion to availability (i.e., the proportion of locations in that cover type is roughly equal to the proportion that occurs in the home range or study area, which makes selection coefficients a little easier to interpret). I usually include very rare cover types (<2% of the landscape) in the reference category unless there is a priori reason to think they are biologically important, if exploratory analysis indicates that the animals really seem to seek them out, or if I am working with very large numbers of locations per animal that ensure that I have enough statistical power to detect biologically meaningful patterns of selection.

messages.subject: Re: Variogram oscillations in shorebird GPS data
messages.subject_clean: Variogram oscillations in shorebird GPS data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

Data gaps can make the variograms look bad. There's a dt argument that can help with that, but it looks like they return to their nest/colony at the end of the day - that's probably the largest behavior that's missing from the model. A daily periodicity might help a little, but what's needed more is the variance expanding and contracting daily, which is not currently coded up. The model looks okay enough without that - the short lags look good, which are what's needed for speed/distance estimation, and the asymptote looks good, which is what's needed for range estimation.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: GPS data from bluetooth trackers
messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the response Chris.

The article by Farine et al. (2024) stated that positional error increased exponentially with reported accuracy estimate (reference image from the article below). The article suggested to apply threshold to detections to avoid majority of large estimation errors. But as a rookie in movement ecology and data analysis, I am unsure with what "applying a threshold" mean exactly. So I removed data points that were beyond an ACC value of 70, which is probably not the best way forward as I arbitrarily decided on that number based on some trials I did by walking with the tags and seeing how accurate the GPS points recorded were.

Since I am trying to answer space use intensity of cats in relation to distance from food source (feeding spots designated by communal cat feeders), I chose not to segment the data and instead to filter out data points with intervals less than 5 minutes. This brought down the data points from ~20k to ~2k (for 1 cat). However, this number was once again arbitrarily defined since according to the sampling interval graph plotted, my dataset does not seem to have a consistent detection interval (red line = 5min).

To summarize I removed time and location duplicates, ACC > 70 and time intervals < 5 min. I used AKDEc to find the 95% home range of the cat. This was the result I got after visualizing it on QGIS, which I think is substantially better than the oval I got initially.

I have also sent over the raw points of the cat’s data with all duplicates (time and location) removed. I am especially unsure about how I should determine an appropriate accuracy threshold and sampling interval rather than choosing these values arbitrarily. It would be greatly appreciated if you are able to inform me if I am doing the analysis correctly or if there any areas I may improve on.

Here is the code used without any form of error corrections.

# Finding best movement model for each data

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(putu,interactive=FALSE)

M.OUF <- ctmm.fit(putu, GUESS)

AKDE_putu <- akde(putu, M.OUF, debias = TRUE)

# Variogram

SVF <- variogram(putu)

level <- 0.95

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Zoomed out

plot(

  SVF,

  CTMM = M.OUF,

  col.CTMM = c("blue", "red", "orange"),

  fraction = 0.65,

  level = level

)

title("long-term variogram")

# Zoomed in

plot(

  SVF,

  CTMM = M.OUF,

  col.CTMM = c("blue", "red", "orange"),

  fraction = 0.1,

  level = level

)

title("short-term variogram")

A follow up question slightly separate from ctmm, but it would be great if you could share some insights if you have experience in this area. If I were to make use of Marzluff et al. (2004) Resource Utilization Function (RUF) to model utilization distribution of space in correlation with distance to food source, would it be appropriate for me to use AKDE's PDF, despite fixed KDE being the most commonly applied technique?

Best,
Yuen Kei

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

I am planning to use ctmm with telemetry data from the brand new Argos-Kinéis satellite constellation. As of this year, Argos data no longer comes with error ellipse variables. This new system instead provides circular error radii (in meters) for all location classes (3, 2, 1, A, and B). Because positions are now estimated using the 20 new Kinéis satellites in addition to the 5 Argos legacy satellites, these error radii are far more accurate than the location class error ranges estimated with the old Least Squares method. Are you aware of this transition with Argos data, and does ctmm have plans to be able to import Argos data in as.telemetry() that have a single error radius column instead of the three error ellipse variables?

Thanks in advance!
Maina

Hi All,

I've been trying to conduct rsf.select on bird home ranges (93 to 378 telemetry locations).

I'm using the cropland raster (https://croplandcros.scinet.usda.gov/) to see what habitats the birds select.  I'm running into issues where my output (the summary function) shows each category as having an est of NaN.

In addition, I am trying to run continuous rasters (percent canopy cover and percent impervious surface), and for some home ranges they are not showing up as having a coefficient (it just shows area, T[position], T[velocity], etc.).

For all rasters, I made sure they matched the projection of the telemetry objects (the bird movebank points and the wAKDE), and I made sure the crop raster was a factor.  I also clipped the rasters to encompass the entire home range with a buffer.

Here is the code I use:

rsf_can_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(canopy=canopy_799),
                                 debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95)
summary(rsf_can_799)

rsf_imp_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(imp=imp_799),
                                 debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95)
summary(rsf_imp_799)

rsf_crop_799 <- ctmm:::rsf.select(bird_799, UD=wAKDE_799, R=list(crop=crop_799),
                                  debias=TRUE, error=0.05, trace=TRUE, level.UD=0.95,
                                  integrator="Riemann")

summary(rsf_crop_799)

If anyone had a similar problem or could provide guidance, it would be greatly appreciated!!!

I feel like I've tried everything to no avail.

Thank you!
